note.overview: Parcel logistics companies use zoning systems to manage last-mile delivery operations. This practice divides a service area into zones, each served by its own station and drivers. Designing an optimal zoning policy is challenging because the practical service area often includes many customer locations, and vehicle routing problems (VRPs) should be incorporated as a subroutine.

Designing an optimal zoning policy is challenging because the practical service area often includes many customer locations, and vehicle routing problems (VRPs) should be incorporated as a subroutine.
The drivers were not informed of any changes in the zoning; they receive packages for their daily routes based on the assignment by the station manager.
We provide the work span and delivery time results in Tables 3 and 4, respectively.

This further stresses that the proposed zoning can help the system operator better manage the workload among drivers and limit the undesirable cases with extremely long working hours, thereby creating a win–win scenario for both the company and its drivers.
Our method iteratively solves VRPs using observed demand data and partitions the region with additively weighted Voronoi diagrams.
